summary.headline: Can Fin Homes FY26 disbursements hit INR10,531 crore, just above guidance, with Q4 a record INR3,245 crore; FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 disbursements of INR10,531 crore marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guidance, with each quarter setting a new peak and Q4 at INR3,245 crore. AUM growth was about 10.44% as rundown ran about INR600 crore above the INR6,000 crore assumption. Karnataka grew 7% in disbursements after e-khata issues, and Telangana ended roughly flat at INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore. Q4 included two one-offs: INR46 crore additional DTA provision on standard assets and INR13.5 crore tax refund gain; management says underlying FY26 profit was INR1,027 crore, up 20% from INR857 crore. Around 85% of the book has moved to quarterly reset, with the 50 bps pass-through and a 15 bps cut in January leaving an opening yield near 9.8% and spread of about 2.8%.

after 50 bps quarterly-reset pass-through and 15 bps January cut

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement growth of 7% after e-khata delays; Q4 averaged about INR290 crore per month; FY27 target is 15% growth. Delinquency is lowest among six zones.

segments.name: Telangana
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursements INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore in FY25, roughly flat; now running INR100 crore-plus per month and expected to be positive from day one of FY27.

segments.name: North and West zones
segments.commentary: Each running about INR150-160 crore per month; North and West together grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: Tamil Nadu
segments.commentary: Running INR180-200 crore per month; growing around 30%.

segments.name: East zone (mainly Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Running close to INR100 crore per month; grew about 40%-plus in FY26 per management.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: Share rose by about 2 percentage points in FY26 as a deliberate push, mainly in Karnataka.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore, about 25% growth, applied roughly uniformly across zones.
FY27 rundown (prepayments, BT outs, closures) assumed at about INR7,000 crore, giving net book addition of about INR6,000 crore and AUM growth of about 14%.
FY27 spread guidance 2.75% and NIM guidance 3.75%, kept conservative versus opening spread of about 2.8%.
FY27 credit cost guidance 15 bps, though management expects it to be well below that.
IT programme: about INR40 crore net incremental cost in FY27 (about INR60 crore of depreciation and opex against about INR20 crore current IT cost); cost-to-income ratio to rise slightly.
FY27 ROA target about 2.4%; ROE expected at 18%-plus, slightly diluted by IT costs.
28 new branches planned for the first half of FY27 (3 in Karnataka, 2 in Telangana); sales team to grow from about 80-90 to about 150.
Employee cost expected to rise about 10%-12% in FY27; other opex from INR134 crore to INR175-180 crore.
capex_capacity: IT transformation totals INR300 crore: INR100 crore capex and INR200 crore opex spread over 5 years; depreciation begins mainly in FY27.
Infrastructure and security modules are complete; deposit applications and HRMS are live; LOS and LMS go live in Q1 FY27 and are expected to drive the next stage of efficiency gains.
Branch network grew by 54 branches over FY23-FY25; 15 branches opened in the first half of FY26 contributed INR863 crore of disbursements versus INR128 crore from earlier branches in FY25.
Sales team of about 80-90 people contributed about INR868 crore in FY26 versus INR183 crore from a team of 30-35 in FY25.
demand_pricing: Demand inquiries remain good across branches; affordable segment has slowed to mid-single-digit growth, while mid and prime segments hold up better.
About 85% of the book is now on quarterly reset (from about 48% annual-reset-to-quarterly shift in Q4); about 15% remains on annual reset and would lag if rates rise.
About 62% of liabilities are bank loans linked to repo; NCDs carry a blended cost of about 7.66%-7.67%; CP rates fell to about 6.45% in April from above 7% in Q4.

Q4 BT outs were about INR400 crore, roughly 25% of the INR1,730 crore total rundown; main competitors for BT outs are LIC Housing and Bajaj Finance, with Bajaj winning mainly on takeover-plus-top-up offers.
Incremental yield is about 9.8% or higher; salaried share of new business fell from about 89% to about 83-84% (self-employed mix rising).
PMAY/CLSS traction is limited: about INR1 lakh crore of PMAY claims across all HFCs and NBFCs in six months, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BT-out and rundown rate peaking after the April quarterly-reset shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q4 to be the peak; BT outs were about INR380-400 crore in Q3 and Q4, nearly flat, and FY27 rundown is modelled at INR7,000 crore versus about INR6,600 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will disbursements reach INR13,000 crore given branch growth of about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are 28 new branches in H1 FY27, expanding the sales team from 80-90 to about 150, and recovery in Karnataka and Telangana; the company is also planning for elevated prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 state-wise disbursement run rates and opex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current monthly run rates: Karnataka about INR275-290 crore, Tamil Nadu INR180-200 crore, North and West INR150-160 crore each, Telangana INR110-120 crore, East about INR100 crore. Employee cost is INR177 crore and other cost INR134 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Are the West Asia situation or LAP delinquencies showing stress, and is any management overlay planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress seen in bounce rates or delinquencies through March and April; no additional management overlay planned, but PCR rose from 49% to 56%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and margins after the reset and NHB repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is expected at about 2.8%, with guidance kept at 2.75%; the only risk is a rate rise, which would affect the roughly 15% of the book still on annual reset.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company losing prepayments to LIC Housing and Bajaj?
qa_highlights.answer: LIC wins on price, offering rates such as 7.15% on new business; Bajaj wins on takeover-plus-top-up, where Can Fin is more conservative on LTV.

risks_watch: Rate-up cycle: about 15% of the book on annual reset would lag repricing, while about 62% of liabilities reprice quickly.
Prepayment pressure from LIC Housing and Bajaj; rundown assumed at INR7,000 crore, and a higher rundown would cut the 14% AUM growth outlook.
Affordable segment demand slowdown, which management acknowledged.
LOS and LMS go-live in Q1 FY27 and the IT cost ramp (about INR40 crore net) could weigh on cost-to-income ratio.
Karnataka e-khata rollout in gram panchayat rural areas is still delayed; Telangana needs to sustain INR100 crore-plus monthly run rate.
Borrowing cost trajectory: NCD refinancing at lower rates and NHB tranche repricing are expected benefits but not yet visible.
summary.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and spread retention, with the 2.8% spread and 15 bps credit cost stated as conservative guidance. Cautious on affordable-segment demand and on prepayment losses to LIC and Bajaj, and some answers were evasive on the exact disbursement and spread drivers.

growth.why: FY27 disbursement target of INR13,000 crore (about 25% growth) implies about 14% AUM growth on a INR7,000 crore rundown assumption; backing is partial, with 28 new branches and sales team expansion from 80-90 to 150 people, but no order-book style contracts and affordable segment slowing to mid-single digits.
